review.primaryContribution: Iranian mathematician whose 2004 Harvard thesis counted simple closed geodesics on hyperbolic surfaces, computed volumes of moduli spaces and gave a new proof of Witten's conjecture, who showed that Thurston's earthquake flow is ergodic and mixing, and who with Alex Eskin and, in part, Amir Mohammadi proved that the closure of a complex geodesic in moduli space is an algebraic subvariety; the International Mathematical Union awarded her the Fields Medal in 2014 for her outstanding contributions to the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces and their moduli spaces, and its press release calls her contributions striking and highly original.
review.topOmission: None identified. The thesis results, the dynamics on moduli space (the earthquake flow and the Eskin-Mirzakhani-Mohammadi theorem) and the Fields Medal are all carded. A reader may expect her work with Elon Lindenstrauss on the space of measured laminations, the counting of closed geodesics in moduli space with Eskin, her Olympiad medals, her Princeton and Stanford posts or her late joint work with Alex Wright; none is a defining contribution beside the three cards.
displayedAchievements: Her 2004 Harvard thesis (adviser Curtis McMullen) counted simple closed geodesics on hyperbolic surfaces (asymptotically a constant times L to the power 6g-6), proved it by calculating volumes in moduli space, and gave a new and completely unexpected proof of Edward Witten's conjecture, first proved by Maxim Kontsevich in 1992; it yielded papers in Annals, Inventiones and the Journal of the AMS

Turned to dynamics on moduli space: the IMU says she found a new construction bridging its holomorphic and symplectic aspects and used it to show Thurston's earthquake flow is ergodic and mixing; with Alex Eskin and, for the orbit-closure part, Amir Mohammadi, she proved that closures of complex geodesics are algebraic subvarieties rather than fractals, a result the IMU compares with Ratner's rigidity theorems and that Wright and Zorich call the Magic Wand Theorem

Awarded the Fields Medal in 2014 for her outstanding contributions to the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces and their moduli spaces; the citation says she made stunning advances and led the way to new frontiers by integrating algebraic geometry, topology and probability theory, and Stanford records her as the first woman to win the medal since it began in 1936
review.notes: First pass: card 1 the thesis (simple closed geodesics, volumes of moduli space, Witten's conjecture), card 2 dynamics on moduli space (the earthquake flow from the IMU release and the Eskin-Mirzakhani-Mohammadi theorem), card 3 the 2014 Fields Medal with the citation and the first-woman fact. The IMU's own summary lists three results (the geodesic counting and Witten's conjecture, the earthquake flow, and the closure of complex geodesics), so the earthquake flow was in card 2 from the first pass rather than added by the gate; the card order follows the mathematics, with the medal last, so the first-woman milestone does not displace the contribution; with the name hidden, the cards explain a mathematician whose thesis settled counting and volume questions on surfaces, who proved rigidity theorems for dynamics on moduli space and who received the field's highest prize. No first-pass failure was found, so correctedBySelfGate is empty; precautions taken while drafting, all traced to a source that states them: the thesis results, the asymptotic form, the calculation of volumes first and the deduction of the count, the 1992 Kontsevich proof, the three journals (IMU release and Quanta); the earthquake flow result and the algebraic-subvariety theorem with the fractal contrast (IMU citation page and release); the Eskin-Mirzakhani-Mohammadi credit (IMU release, Quanta) so the card does not present the theorem as hers alone; the comparison with Ratner (IMU release); the Magic Wand name and its wide use (Wright and Zorich in the Notices); the Fields Medal citation, the stunning advances wording and the quality list (IMU pages); and the first-woman claim in the form Stanford's obituary states it (the first woman to win the Fields Medal since its inception in 1936). Not used as facts: Farb's opinion that the Eskin-Mirzakhani work is probably the theorem of the decade and the 'monumental' wording (Quanta), the Stanford start year (the sources give 2008 and 2009) and any honours list beyond the medal. Excluded throughout: her illness and death, family and private life, political and social views, and any nationalism; her Iranian origin appears only as a descriptor in the primary-contribution line, not as a theme of any card. Significance over novelty: the doodling method and the persistence episodes are confined to Moments and the Turning Point. Side projects: her Olympiad medals, Princeton and Stanford posts, committee and editorial service and her late work with Alex Wright are not carded. Self-calibration: seven of nine scored rows were lowered before return (creative originality, intuitive synthesis, curiosity, persistence, deep focus, collaboration, mastery orientation). Portrait is held (see the candidate file).

achievements.en: Mirzakhani's 2004 doctoral thesis at Harvard, supervised by Curtis McMullen, answered a long-standing question about counting simple closed geodesics on hyperbolic surfaces: on a surface of genus g their number below length L grows like a constant times L to the power 6g-6. She proved it by calculating volumes in moduli space, the space of all hyperbolic structures on a surface, and the same approach gave a new and completely unexpected proof of Edward Witten's conjecture, which Maxim Kontsevich had first proved in 1992. The thesis yielded papers in Annals of Mathematics, Inventiones Mathematicae and the Journal of the American Mathematical Society.
achievements.ko: 미르자카니는 커티스 맥멀런의 지도로 쓴 2004년 하버드 대학교 박사 논문에서 쌍곡 곡면 위의 단순 닫힌 측지선을 세는 오랜 문제에 답했다. 종수가 g인 곡면에서 길이가 L 이하인 단순 닫힌 측지선의 수가 어떤 상수에 L의 6g−6제곱을 곱한 값처럼 늘어난다는 것을 보인 것이다. 그는 곡면의 모든 쌍곡 구조를 모은 모듈라이 공간의 부피를 계산하는 방식으로 이를 증명했고, 같은 접근으로 1992년 막심 콘체비치가 처음 증명한 에드워드 위튼의 추측에 대해 전혀 뜻밖의 새로운 증명도 얻었다. 이 논문은 《Annals of Mathematics》, 《Inventiones Mathematicae》, 《Journal of the American Mathematical Society》에 실린 세 편의 논문으로 이어졌다.

achievements.en: Mirzakhani then turned to dynamics on moduli space. The International Mathematical Union says she found a new construction bridging the holomorphic and symplectic aspects of moduli space and used it to show that Thurston's earthquake flow is ergodic and mixing. With Alex Eskin and, for the orbit-closure part, Amir Mohammadi, she then proved that the closure of a complex geodesic in moduli space is always an algebraic subvariety rather than a fractal, a result the Union compares with Marina Ratner's rigidity theorems for homogeneous spaces. Alex Wright and Anton Zorich call it the Magic Wand Theorem and say that most recent papers in the area use it in one way or another.
achievements.ko: 이후 미르자카니는 모듈라이 공간 위의 동역학으로 눈을 돌렸다. 국제수학연맹(IMU)에 따르면 그는 모듈라이 공간의 정칙적 측면과 심플렉틱 측면을 잇는 새로운 구성을 찾아냈고, 이를 이용해 서스턴의 지진 흐름이 에르고딕이며 혼합적임을 보였다. 이어 앨릭스 에스킨, 그리고 궤도 폐포 부분에서는 아미르 모하마디와 함께, 모듈라이 공간에서 복소 측지선의 폐포가 프랙털이 아니라 언제나 대수적 부분다양체임을 증명했다. 국제수학연맹은 이 결과를 마리나 래트너가 동차 공간에서 이룬 강성 정리에 견준다. 앨릭스 라이트와 안톤 조리치는 이를 '마법 지팡이 정리'라 부르며, 이 분야의 최근 논문 대부분이 어떤 식으로든 이 정리를 쓴다고 말한다.

achievements.en: In 2014 the International Mathematical Union awarded Mirzakhani the Fields Medal for her outstanding contributions to the dynamics and geometry of Riemann surfaces and their moduli spaces. Its citation says she made stunning advances and led the way to new frontiers by integrating methods from algebraic geometry, topology and probability theory, and its press release credits her with a rare combination of superb technical ability, bold ambition, far-reaching vision and deep curiosity. Stanford records that she was the first woman to win the medal since it began in 1936.
achievements.ko: 2014년 국제수학연맹(IMU)은 미르자카니에게 리만 곡면과 그 모듈라이 공간의 동역학과 기하학에 대한 뛰어난 공헌을 인정해 필즈상을 수여했다. 수상 이유서는 그가 대수기하학, 위상수학, 확률론의 방법을 통합해 눈부신 진전을 이루고 이 분야의 새로운 전선을 열었다고 밝히며, 보도자료는 그를 뛰어난 기술적 능력과 대담한 야심, 먼 안목, 깊은 호기심을 두루 갖춘 드문 수학자로 평가한다. 스탠퍼드 대학교는 그가 1936년 제정된 이래 필즈상을 받은 첫 번째 여성이었다고 전한다.

moments.en: While still a graduate student at Harvard, Mirzakhani heard about Curtis McMullen's result on the orbits of translation surfaces of genus two and, before his paper was published, came to his office and asked why he had done just genus two. McMullen, who tells the story to Quanta, says that what she sees hints of, she wants to understand more clearly. Years later, after several projects together, she and Alex Eskin, partly with Amir Mohammadi, succeeded in 2012 and 2013 in extending his result to all surfaces with more than two holes.
moments.ko: 미르자카니는 하버드 대학원생이던 시절, 커티스 맥멀런이 종수 2인 병진 곡면(translation surface)의 궤도에 관한 결과를 내놓았다는 소식을 듣고, 그의 논문이 발표되기도 전에 연구실로 찾아가 왜 종수 2인 경우만 다루었느냐고 물었다. 맥멀런은 퀀타 매거진과의 인터뷰에서 이 일화를 들려주며, 그가 어렴풋이 본 것을 더 분명히 이해하고 싶어 하는 사람이라고 말했다. 그로부터 여러 해 뒤, 몇 차례의 공동 연구를 거친 끝에 미르자카니는 앨릭스 에스킨, 그리고 일부는 아미르 모하마디와 함께 2012~2013년에 이 결과를 구멍이 둘보다 많은 모든 곡면으로 확장하는 데 성공했다.
moments.interpretationEn: This is consistent with a mathematician drawn to the general question behind a solved special case, though the anecdote is McMullen's recollection in a profile, and the later theorem was a joint effort of three authors after years of work.
moments.interpretationKo: 이미 풀린 특수한 경우 뒤에 있는 일반적인 질문에 이끌리는 수학자의 모습과 일치하지만, 이 일화는 인터뷰에서 맥멀런이 회상한 것이며 이후의 정리는 세 저자가 여러 해에 걸쳐 함께 이룬 공동 작업이다.

moments.en: Alex Eskin describes the project with Mirzakhani on orbit closures in moduli space: after about two years of work they realised that a fact they could not prove blocked their path. They looked for a way to repair the argument for more than a year without progress, kept talking once a week, and then found a different approach based on a relative of a method they had learned from Elon Lindenstrauss; it took another two years to work out the details. Quanta quotes Eskin that when there were setbacks she never panicked, and quotes her own remark that she does not give up easily.
moments.ko: 앨릭스 에스킨은 미르자카니와 함께한 모듈라이 공간의 궤도 폐포 연구를 이렇게 회고한다. 약 2년 동안 연구한 뒤 증명하지 못하는 사실 하나가 길을 가로막고 있음을 깨달았다. 두 사람은 1년 넘게 논증을 고칠 방법을 찾았지만 진전이 없었고, 그러는 동안에도 일주일에 한 번씩 계속 대화를 나누었다. 그러다 엘론 린덴슈트라우스에게 배운 방법의 친척뻘인 다른 접근을 찾아냈고, 세부 사항을 정리하는 데 다시 2년이 걸렸다. 퀀타 매거진은 에스킨이 차질이 생겨도 그가 당황한 적이 없었다고 말했다고 전하고, 미르자카니 자신은 쉽게 포기하지 않는다고 말했다고 전한다.
moments.interpretationEn: This is consistent with persistence on a long, difficult problem, though it is told by her collaborator in a memorial tribute, and both the 'never panicked' remark and her own 'I don't give up easily' are read through a single profile.
moments.interpretationKo: 길고 어려운 문제를 붙들고 버티는 모습과 일치하지만, 이 이야기는 공동 연구자가 추모 글에서 전한 것이며 '당황하지 않았다'는 말과 본인의 '쉽게 포기하지 않는다'는 말은 모두 하나의 인물 기사를 통해 전해진다.

turningPoints.en: After the thesis, whose results came from hyperbolic geometry, Mirzakhani spent 2004-2008 as a Clay Research Fellow and assistant professor at Princeton, a fellowship she says gave her the freedom to think about harder problems, travel and talk to other mathematicians, without having to write up her work in a rush. Elon Lindenstrauss, who met her there in 2004, recalls that she was already dreaming of classifying the invariant measures and orbit closures for the action of SL(2,R) on moduli space, a quest that was somewhat speculative at the time, and Eskin recalls that their joint work began with vague dreams and no concrete plan. The IMU sums up the shift: her early results in hyperbolic geometry brought widespread recognition, and her most recent work is a major advance in dynamical systems.
turningPoints.ko: 박사 논문의 성과가 쌍곡 기하학에서 나온 뒤, 미르자카니는 2004년부터 2008년까지 프린스턴 대학교에서 클레이 연구 펠로이자 조교수로 지냈다. 그는 이 펠로십 덕분에 더 어려운 문제를 생각하고, 자유롭게 여행하고, 다른 수학자들과 이야기할 자유를 얻었으며 연구를 서둘러 정리하지 않아도 되었다고 말한다. 2004년 프린스턴에서 그를 만난 엘론 린덴슈트라우스는 당시 그가 이미 모듈라이 공간 위 SL(2,R) 작용의 불변 측도와 궤도 폐포를 분류하는 꿈을 꾸고 있었고 이는 당시로서는 다소 투기적인 시도였다고 회고하며, 에스킨은 두 사람의 공동 연구가 막연한 꿈에서, 구체적인 계획 없이 시작되었다고 기억한다. 국제수학연맹은 이 변화를 이렇게 요약한다. 초기의 쌍곡 기하학 결과로 폭넓은 인정을 받았고, 가장 최근의 연구는 동역학계에서의 중요한 진전이라는 것이다.
turningPoints.interpretationEn: This is consistent with a mathematician willing to commit to a goal with no known route, though the IMU describes the geometry and the dynamics as parts of one programme on moduli space, and the 'dreaming' recollections come from tribute writers after her death.
turningPoints.interpretationKo: 구체적인 길이 보이지 않는 목표에 몰두하는 수학자의 모습과 일치하지만, 국제수학연맹은 기하학과 동역학을 모듈라이 공간을 둘러싼 하나의 연구 흐름으로 설명하며, '꿈꾸었다'는 회고는 사후에 쓰인 추모 글에서 나온 것이다.
